instruments.name: Kick Drum
instruments.description: Synthesized kick drum driving the four-on-the-floor pulse of this 80s techno track (tracks "Kick" and "Syncopated Kick"). The foundational rhythmic anchor at 126 BPM.

patch.name: Kick Drum
patch.description: Single sine oscillator through a Standard low-pass filter at 1 kHz with no resonance, into a VCA. Two snappy ADSR envelopes (attack 1 ms, decay 50 ms, zero sustain) give the punchy click-and-thump body with no tail.

instruments.name: Snare Drum
instruments.description: Snare drum for the backbeat (track "Snare"), providing the 2-and-4 accent that propels the 80s techno groove.

patch.name: Snare Drum
patch.description: A tonal triangle oscillator and a white-noise generator mixed together, then through a Standard low-pass filter at 5 kHz with moderate resonance (0.3). Two short ADSR envelopes (attack 1 ms, decay 30 to 120 ms, zero sustain) shape the tuned body and the noisy crack.

instruments.name: Hi-Hat
instruments.description: Hi-hat used for the driving sixteenth-note top end and ticking percussion (tracks "Hats" and "Percussion/Sticks"), keeping the high-frequency motion in this 80s techno arrangement.

patch.name: Hi-Hat
patch.description: Pure white noise through a Standard low-pass filter at 7.5 kHz with resonance 0.4, into a VCA at 0.5. A very fast ADSR (attack 1 ms, decay 50 ms, release 30 ms, zero sustain) produces the tight, bright tick.

instruments.name: Aggressive Bass
instruments.description: Aggressive lead bass carrying the main bassline (track "Bass"), the punchy mid-forward groove element that locks with the kick in this 80s techno track.

patch.name: Aggressive Bass
patch.description: A square oscillator plus a sine Sub Oscillator one octave down for weight, through a Standard low-pass filter at 300 Hz with resonance 0.4. Two ADSR envelopes (attack ~3 ms, decay 200 to 300 ms, sustain 20 to 70 percent) shape the aggressive, plucky-yet-sustained tone.

instruments.name: Vintage Lead
instruments.description: Main monophonic-style synth lead for the "Lead" track, carrying the song's primary Jarre-style melodic hook over the 80s techno groove. Bright, slightly hollow vintage analog lead with subtle vibrato for an expressive retro-electro top line.

patch.name: Vintage Lead
patch.description: Two oscillators mixed: a sawtooth (level 0.6) plus a 30% pulse-width pulse (level 0.4) for a hollow vintage tone. Standard-model lowpass filter at 2 kHz with moderate resonance (0.4), shaped by a fast-attack ADSR (2 ms attack, 0.2 s decay, 40% sustain). LFO 1 is a 5.5 Hz sine at tiny depth (0.015) for gentle vibrato, and LFO 2 is a slow 0.4 Hz triangle (depth 0.35) for a drifting pulse-width/tone movement.

instruments.name: Analog Dream Machine
instruments.description: Lush evolving pad for the "Pad" track, providing the warm sustained harmonic bed underneath the 80s techno arrangement in classic Jean-Michel Jarre fashion. Slow-swelling, detuned analog pad that fills the background and glues the chords together.

patch.name: Analog Dream Machine
patch.description: Two sawtooth oscillators mixed with the second detuned +8 ct for a wide, warm analog beating. Standard-model lowpass filter at 800 Hz with moderate resonance (0.5) keeps it soft and dark. A very slow ADSR (0.8 s attack, 1.0 s decay, 75% sustain, 2.0 s release) gives the gentle swell and long tail, and a looping 6-segment MSEG modulator adds slow evolving movement over the sustained tone.

instruments.name: Sub Bass
instruments.description: Sub bass holding the low-frequency harmonic foundation (track "Sub Bass (Harmony)"), reinforcing the root notes beneath the main bass in this 80s techno track.

patch.name: Sub Bass
patch.description: A sawtooth oscillator combined with a sine Sub Oscillator one octave down, through a Standard low-pass filter at 400 Hz with resonance 0.6. A sustaining ADSR (attack 2 ms, decay 150 ms, sustain 60 percent, release 100 ms) keeps the deep, steady low end.

instruments.name: Unison Supersaw
instruments.description: Wide unison supersaw lead variation on the "Unison Supersaw (Lead Var)" track, used as a thicker, detuned alternative voicing of the main lead for big retro-electro lead moments and choruses in this 80s techno track.

patch.name: Unison Supersaw
patch.description: Single sawtooth oscillator running 7-voice unison with 25 ct detune and full stereo spread (1.0) for a classic wide supersaw. Standard-model lowpass filter open at 1.8 kHz with low resonance (0.15) keeps it bright, and a sustained ADSR (5 ms attack, 0.4 s decay, 70% sustain, 0.3 s release) lets chords and lead notes ring. No LFO modulation; the movement comes entirely from the unison detune.

instruments.name: Noise Sweep
instruments.description: Noise Sweep (SFX): a slow filtered-noise riser/whoosh used as a transitional sweep between sections of this 80s techno track, building tension into drops and breakdowns Jarre-style.

patch.name: Noise Sweep
patch.description: Pink noise source into a Standard low-pass filter (cutoff 1.5 kHz, resonance 0.7) for a focused colored sweep. A slow sine LFO (0.2 Hz, depth 0.8) modulates to animate the sweep, and a long ADSR (0.5 s attack, 1 s release) gives a smooth swelling whoosh.

instruments.name: Shepard Riser
instruments.description: Shepard Riser (SFX): an endlessly-rising tone used as a build-up effect to create perpetual upward motion and tension before drops in this 80s techno arrangement.

patch.name: Shepard Riser
patch.description: Math Oscillator set to the Shepard algorithm (Param A 0.5, Param B 0.7) for the classic illusion of infinite ascent. Routed through a Standard low-pass filter (cutoff 4 kHz, low resonance 0.1) to soften the top, with a slow ADSR (1 s attack, 2 s release) for a gradual swell.

instruments.name: Pluck Synth
instruments.description: Short plucky synth for the "Arpeggio" track, driving the song's rhythmic arpeggiated 16th-note motion in the classic Jarre / 80s techno style. Tight, percussive note attacks that keep the arpeggio crisp and rhythmic.

patch.name: Pluck Synth
patch.description: Single sawtooth oscillator into a Standard-model lowpass filter at 1 kHz with moderate resonance (0.45). The plucky character comes from the ADSR: 2 ms attack, 0.2 s decay, 0% sustain and 0.15 s release, so each note decays to silence for a staccato arpeggio. No unison or LFO modulation.

instruments.name: Resonant Percussion
instruments.description: Resonant percussion hit for accents and transitions (track "Impact FX"), adding metallic Jarre-style impacts that punctuate sections of the 80s techno arrangement.

patch.name: Resonant Percussion
patch.description: A Mechanical Noise generator in Hammer mode (15 ms duration, 5 kHz cutoff, high velocity sensitivity) into a VCA. A medium ADSR (attack 1 ms, decay 300 ms, release 200 ms, zero sustain) gives the resonant, ringing impact tail.

instruments.name: Euclidean Texture
instruments.description: Euclidean Texture (Intro Textures): a self-generating rhythmic/melodic texture that supplies evolving intro atmosphere and arpeggiated movement, a Jarre-flavoured generative backdrop for this 80s techno piece.

patch.name: Euclidean Texture
patch.description: Generative voice: a Euclidean sequencer (16 steps, 5 pulses, rotation 2, light swing) drives gates while a Turing Machine (Pentatonic scale, length 16) supplies evolving pitch, with Random Gates (density 0.25) adding variation. A Sawtooth Oscillator plus a Math Oscillator feed a Standard low-pass filter (cutoff 2 kHz, resonance 0.25) with a triangle LFO (1.5 Hz) for motion, plucky ADSR (1 ms attack, 0.5 s release), and a Phase Vocoder effect for spectral smearing.

instruments.name: Screamer Lead
instruments.description: Aggressive screaming power lead for the "Screamer Power Lead" track, used for high-energy lead stabs and climactic lines that cut through the 80s techno mix with a hard, resonant edge.

patch.name: Screamer Lead
patch.description: Single sawtooth oscillator through the Screamer filter model at 800 Hz with high resonance (0.72) and heavy drive (2.5) for a screaming, distorted edge. A fast plucky ADSR (1 ms attack, 0.18 s decay, 10% sustain, 0.1 s release) gives sharp stabs, and the Mod Matrix routes Envelope 2 into filter cutoff at amount 0.8 for an aggressive per-note filter sweep.

instruments.name: Wave Folder Bass
instruments.description: Wave Folder Bass (Wavefolder Pressure Bass): an aggressive, harmonically dense bass that anchors the low end of this 80s techno track with gritty, pressurized weight and bite.

patch.name: Wave Folder Bass
patch.description: Math Oscillator on the Wave Folder algorithm (Param A 0.4, Param B 0.3) generates rich folded harmonics, with a CV input on Param A for fold modulation. A Standard low-pass filter (cutoff 600 Hz, resonance 0.4) keeps it sub-focused, driven by a snappy ADSR (1 ms attack, 20% sustain, 0.1 s release). A Distortion effect (drive 0.5, tone 0.8, full mix) adds grit and bite.

instruments.name: Hybrid Resonator
instruments.description: Hybrid Resonator (Harmonic Echo Resonator): a complex multi-oscillator lead/pad hybrid providing the shimmering, metallic-resonant melodic centerpiece of this 80s techno track, rich and Jarre-esque in character.

patch.name: Hybrid Resonator
patch.description: A 16-module hybrid: a Sawtooth Oscillator (4-voice unison, 18 ct detune), a Sub Oscillator (square, -1 oct), a Math Oscillator on the BitWise algorithm, a Wavetable (Basic table, position 0.25) and a touch of White Noise are blended through two Mixers. The sum runs into a Ring Mod (220 Hz carrier, 45% mix, key tracking) and a Body Resonance (280 Hz, 70% resonance) for the metallic echo character, then a Standard low-pass filter (cutoff 1.2 kHz, resonance 0.35, drive 1.2). A 4 Hz triangle LFO adds movement, a Keyboard Panner spreads notes across the stereo field, and two ADSR envelopes shape amp and tone.

instruments.name: Moog Resonant Sweep
instruments.description: Moog Resonant Sweep: an empty/unused patch with no modules. Not assigned to any track; kept as a placeholder.

patch.name: Moog Resonant Sweep
patch.description: Empty patch: currently contains no modules. Reserved as a placeholder for a future Moog-style resonant filter sweep but presently has no oscillators, filters, envelopes, or effects and produces no sound.

song.name: Oxygene Dreams (80s Techno)
song.description: "Oxygene Dreams (80s Techno)" - an instrumental retro-electro / 80s techno track at 126 BPM, 4/4, about 3:03, with a Jean-Michel Jarre style synth flavour. A four-on-the-floor electronic kit (kick, snare, hi-hats, plus a syncopated kick and stick percussion) drives the groove under an aggressive synth bass and a harmonic sub bass. Melodic content comes from a vintage analog lead, a unison supersaw lead variation, a plucky arpeggio and a wide analog pad, with more experimental voices adding colour (a screamer power lead, a wavefolder pressure bass, a hybrid echo resonator and a euclidean intro texture). Sound-design and transition FX (noise sweeps, a shepard riser, resonant impacts) mark the section changes and build energy. Mood: nostalgic, hypnotic and driving, classic analog-synth nostalgia with a modern techno pulse.
